topic: If I were you, I’d talk to her first

lines.en: Hey, Paloma! You have been quiet all evening. Is something wrong, or are you just tired?
lines.pt: Ei, Paloma! Você está quieta a noite toda. Tem algo errado, ou só está cansada?

lines.en: Honestly, I had an argument with my cousin yesterday. She borrowed some money in June and has not paid me back.
lines.pt: Sinceramente, briguei com minha prima ontem. Ela pegou dinheiro emprestado em junho e ainda não me pagou.

lines.en: That is awkward. Have you asked her directly, or did you only drop hints and hope she would remember?
lines.pt: Que situação chata. Você pediu diretamente, ou só deu indiretas e esperou que ela lembrasse?

lines.en: I dropped hints for weeks. Yesterday I lost my temper and said some things I regret. Now we are not talking.
lines.pt: Dei indiretas por semanas. Ontem perdi a paciência e disse coisas das quais me arrependo. Agora não estamos nos falando.

lines.en: Well, if I were you, I would talk to her first. Waiting for her call will only make things worse.
lines.pt: Bem, se eu fosse você, falaria com ela primeiro. Esperar que ela ligue só vai piorar as coisas.

lines.en: But why should I be the one to apologise? She is the one who owes me money, after all.
lines.pt: Mas por que eu deveria pedir desculpas? Ela é quem me deve dinheiro, afinal.

lines.en: You could apologise only for the shouting, not for the request. That way you keep your dignity and the door stays open.
lines.pt: Você poderia se desculpar só pelos gritos, não pelo pedido. Assim mantém a dignidade e a porta fica aberta.

lines.en: That is clever. Do you think I should write her a message, or would it be better to meet?
lines.pt: Isso é inteligente. Você acha que devo escrever uma mensagem, ou seria melhor nos encontrarmos pessoalmente?

lines.en: Why not invite her for lunch on Saturday? If I were you, I would avoid writing, because messages sound much colder.
lines.pt: Por que não convidá-la para almoçar no sábado? Se eu fosse você, evitaria escrever, porque mensagens soam mais frias do que se pretende.

lines.en: Okay, I will try. And you had better not tell my mother, or the whole family will get involved.
lines.pt: Certo, vou tentar. E é melhor você não contar à minha mãe, ou a família inteira vai se meter.

lines.en: Do not worry, my lips are sealed. Let me make some tea while you call her. You will feel better.
lines.pt: Não se preocupe, minha boca é um túmulo. Vou fazer chá enquanto você liga para ela. Vai se sentir melhor.

facts.big: if I were you · you could · you’d better · why not
facts.label: Dar conselhos
facts.sub: Se eu fosse você, I’d + verbo base. Use you could para opções, you’d better para avisos e why not para sugerir de forma leve.

facts.label: Se eu fosse você
facts.sub: If I were you, I’d + verbo base: If I were you, I’d talk to her first. Em inglês formal usa-se were com todas as pessoas. É o jeito mais comum de aconselhar.

facts.label: Você poderia
facts.sub: You could + verbo base apresenta uma opção sem forçar: You could apologise only for the shouting. Use quando há mais de uma saída possível.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: “If I were you” is used to give advice.
items.why: It imagines the other person’s situation.

items.s: After “If I were you”, we use “I would”.
items.why: If I were you, I would talk to her.

items.s: “You’d better” is a very soft suggestion.
items.why: It is stronger and can sound like a warning.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: “If I were you” is used to give advice. → Verdadeiro (It imagines the other person’s situation.)
After “If I were you”, we use “I would”. → Verdadeiro (If I were you, I would talk to her.)
“You’d better” is a very soft suggestion. → Falso (It is stronger and can sound like a warning.)

pages.title: A friend’s advice · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a cold evening in a warm apartment in Chicago. Paloma sits on the sofa with a blanket. She has been quiet for hours. Her friend Carl notices something is wrong. He puts his book down. He asks her to tell him everything.

“Hey, Paloma! You have been quiet all evening. Is something wrong, or are you just tired?” says Carl. “Honestly, I had an argument with my cousin yesterday. She borrowed some money in June and has not paid me back.” says Paloma. “That is awkward. Have you asked her directly, or did you only drop hints and hope she would remember?” says Carl.
